predecessors.name: Sosso Empire
predecessors.text: 'When the Soso empire collapsed, the entire Kaniaga region was incorporated into Sundiata's Mali Empire'

ledger.x: c. 1235: Sundiata Keita defeats Soumaoro at Kirina and founds the Mali Empire. 'The empire was founded by Sundiata Keita (c. 1214 - c. 1255)'; 'defeated the Sosso army at the Battle of Kirina in approximately 1235'; infobox 'c. 1235 to 1610'. Cliopatria's 1236 start is kept.

c. 1235: the Sosso lands pass to Sundiata. 'When the Soso empire collapsed, the entire Kaniaga region was incorporated into Sundiata's Mali Empire.' The Sundiata page has Sundiata take control of the former Sosso states. The Sosso dossier's loss is dated 1235, Cliopatria's Mali shape begins 1236.
Undated, within Sundiata's reign (c.
ledger.cp: Diafunu and Kita (local chiefdoms; the page names no state)

ledger.x: Undated, within Sundiata's reign: Senegambia and Kaabu are conquered under his general Tiramakhan.
ledger.cp: Senegambian chieftaincies (the page names the Bainuk king Kikikor)

ledger.x: Undated, within Sundiata's reign: Jolof is made a Mali vassal.
Undated, under Sundiata's generals: the northern marches Oualata and Audaghost are taken.
ledger.cp: Oualata and Audaghost (holders not named on the page)

ledger.x: c. 1285: Mali conquers Takrur. 'Around 1286, the Mali Empire conquered Takrur and put it under a military dictatorship ruled by farba (governors)'; infobox 'Conquered and vassalized by Mali Empire: c. 1285'. The Mali page lists Takrur among the northern marches reached by Sundiata's generals, undated; the dated Takrur…

c. 1300: Mali takes Gao. 'Gao had become prosperous enough to attract the Mali Empire's attention' around 1300, and Mali 'took the city and collected taxes until the 1430s'. The Mali page says Gao 'was annexed into the Mali Empire by either Mansa Sakura or Mansa Musa'; Mansa Musa page: Saghmanja conquered Gao…
1324: Mansa Musa annexes Timbuktu peacefully on his way to Mecca.

c. 1360: Jolof becomes permanently independent of Mali. 'Jolof was a vassal of the Mali Empire for much of its early history'; 'the Jolof became permanently independent during a succession dispute c. 1360' (Ogot); Mali page 'During this period the Jolof Empire was founded, and soon dominated all of northern…
1433: the Tuareg take Timbuktu.

c. 1430s: Gao leaves Mali. Infobox 'Independence from Mali Empire: c. 1430s'; Mali had taken the city and 'collected taxes until the 1430s'. The Mali page puts the area around Gao independent of Malian control after the 1370s war with the Tuareg of Takedda, and the Songhai page says dynastic instability in the 1380s…
c. 1436: the Tuareg take Oualata. 'Three years later, Oualata also fell into their hands', three years after 1433-1434.
1465: Songhai conquers Mema.
Page silent on Mali for 1475; the Cliopatria shape drops to 13.9 N.
1502: Songhai takes Diafunu.
1537: Kaabu breaks away.
By 1576: Mali reasserts authority over Wuli on the north bank of the Gambia.
The Gambian suzerainty ends with the empire; the page gives no separate date.

c. 1610: the Mali Empire ends with Mahmud Keita IV. 'Around 1610, Mahmud Keita IV died'; 'No single Keita ever ruled Manden after Mahmud Keita IV's death, resulting in the end of the Mali Empire'; 'Kangaba became the last refuge of the Keita royal family'.

wars.name: Battle of Kirina
wars.outcome: Sundiata's coalition defeated the Sosso under Soumaoro; Mali founded and the Sosso lands incorporated.

wars.name: Mali-Tuareg war at Gao
wars.outcome: 'In the 1370s a war between Mali imperial forces and Berber Tuareg forces from Takedda devastated the city of Gao.

wars.name: Tuareg capture of Timbuktu and Oualata
wars.outcome: The Tuareg took Timbuktu in 1433-34 and Oualata three years later.

wars.name: Songhai conquest of Mema and Timbuktu
wars.outcome: Songhai took Mema in 1465 and Timbuktu (from the Tuareg) in 1468.

wars.name: Songhai attack on Diafunu
wars.outcome: Askia Muhammad I's forces defeated the Mali general Fati Quali Keita and seized the province of Diafunu.

wars.name: Songhai sack of the Mali capital
wars.outcome: The Songhai under kanfari Dawud sacked the capital 'in 1544 or 1545' but 'did not maintain their hold on the Malian capital'; no territory changed hands.

wars.name: Mali attack on Jenne (Moroccan-held)
wars.outcome: Mahmud IV tried to capture Jenne after Songhai's fall (Tondibi 1591) and was beaten on 26 April 1599; he escaped.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a Mali frontier.
